# `type` standard library

The `type` module exposes predicates over the compile-time `Type` value. They
are evaluated while compiling and disappear with their `Type` arguments;
`Type` values never exist at runtime.

| Predicate | True for |
|---|---|
| `is_record` | record shapes |
| `is_enum` | enums |
| `is_ram` | ramifications |
| `is_fn` | function types |
| `is_unit` | Unit |
| `is_homogeneous` | homogeneous records |
| `is_indexable` | indexable shapes |
| `is_iterable` | iterable shapes |
| `is_array` | growable arrays |
| `is_slice` | slices |
| `is_map` | maps |
| `is_scalar` | scalar types |
| `is_int` | integer types |
| `is_float` | floating-point types |
| `is_numeric` | integer or floating-point types |
| `is_pointer` | pointer-shaped types |

Every predicate has the declaration `Type => <>` and returns a bare flag.
Use it with a compile-time type parameter rather than a runtime value:

```dva
#use type

numeric: #! T: Type, T => <>
numeric = _ => type::is_numeric(T)
```

The function bodies in `std/type.dva` are placeholders recognized by the
compiler. Their literal source return values do not define runtime behavior.
